members.name: round_number_reversal_v1
members.thesis: Round numbers (multiples of 50 or 100 for NIFTY, multiples of 10/50/100 for stocks) act as psychological support/resistance because traders cluster limit orders and stops at these levels. When price approaches a round number with declining momentum, the order cluster absorbs the move and reverses it
members.exit_stop: 0.2% beyond the round number (if round is support, stop 0.2% below)
filters: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
prefer reversals aligned with VWAP direction
weaknesses: When a round number breaks with volume, the reversal bet fails hard. Stop-hunting at round numbers is also common — market makers exploit this.
Thin per-trade edge (20 bps). High sensitivity to cost assumptions.
Definition of 'round number' is arbitrary — should you use 50s, 100s, 500s? The choice affects signal frequency and quality in hard-to-predict ways.
members.prior_art: Round number / psychological level trading. Widely discussed. See: behavioral finance literature on anchoring (Kahneman & Tversky).

members.name: psychological_level_mean_reversion
members.thesis: Exploits round-number bias. Retail stop-loss orders and limit orders cluster at levels like 500, 1000, 1500. This creates artificial resistance/support. Price often 'pierces' these levels to hunt liquidity and then reverts. This is a behavioral constraint of retail-heavy markets like India.
weaknesses: Levels can 'blow through' during strong news
Requires high liquidity to exit at round numbers
